title: 💡 Allow window.focus() between same-origin tabs

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

Currently, web applications cannot programmatically bring another open tab to the foreground using window.focus(), even if both tabs belong to the same origin.

This restriction exists for security reasons, but in scenarios where a web system relies on multiple tabs (e.g., an admin panel with a dashboard and multiple sub-pages), it creates a usability issue:

A user clicks a button in Tab B, expecting Tab A (the main menu) to be highlighted, but there is no way to programmatically focus it.

### What solutions exist today?

Since we cannot use window.focus(), developers are forced to use:

Title blinking (document.title changes) – not ideal and can be ignored.
LocalStorage or BroadcastChannel – allows communication but doesn’t bring the tab to the foreground.

### How would you solve it?

I propose allowing window.focus() between tabs of the same origin, but with a user-driven constraint to prevent abuse.

Security Considerations:
window.focus() should be allowed only for tabs that were opened via window.open() from the same origin.
The focus request should require a user interaction (e.g., a click or keypress event).

### Anything else?

Use Cases:

Enterprise Web Systems:

Many business applications open different modules in separate tabs. The main tab (menu) should be able to regain focus when necessary.
Collaboration Tools:

A web-based IDE or project management system where a tab should bring another relevant tab into focus when switching between tasks.
Web Apps with Multiple Workspaces:

Email clients or messaging apps that allow multiple conversations in different tabs but need a way to refocus the primary tab when a response is received.

Would it be possible to introduce a controlled way to allow tab-to-tab focusing for same-origin pages?
